text.p: Thomson Multimedia is planning to restructure some of its international operations ahead of the privatisation of its parent Thomson SA, afternoon daily Le Monde reported on Saturday.

Le Monde also said France's Lagardere conglomerate and the Alcatel Alsthom engineering group, who are rival bidders for Thomson SA, would give their offers for the privatisation to the finance ministry on Monday morning.
The paper said Thomson Multimedia would use 1.2 billion francs in provisions set aside in its first-half results to carry out the reorganisation.
Citing several unamed sources, the paper said Thomson Multimedia was planning to close eight sites in the United States, Germany and Southeast Asia.
The restructuring, which would not affect operations in France, would result in the loss of about 5,000 jobs from a workforce of 49,500, the paper said.
Le Monde said Thomson Multimedia declined all comment on Friday and no one at the company was available for comment on Saturday.
A government official said on September 12 the government will decide infive or six weeks who will buy the company.
Lagardere has said it will sell Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo Electronics if it wins the bidding.

Thomson SA owns 58 percent of defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF and 100 percent of Thomson Multimedia. The government announced in February that it would privatise Thomson SA as part of a state restructuring of the defence industry.
